author: Alex Kienlen
title: Latest report shows Arkansas gas prices dropping even as crude oil prices stay high - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Kienlen ,
1 hours ago
LITTLE ROCK, Ark. – AAA's latest Arkansas gas prices report shows gasoline prices dropping in the Natural State even as crude prices remain high.
The Thursday report shows drivers in Arkansas are paying 5 cents less per gallon for unleaded regular than they were a week ago. The current $3.88 state average, however, remains above last year's $2.64 average.
Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz as fears grow of return to war West Memphis had the state's highest average gas price at $3.95 per gallon, while Hot Springs had the lowest at $3.67. The national average was $4.27 per gallon, down 6 cents from last week and up $1.21 from a year earlier.
For central Arkansas, Pine Bluff drivers are slightly above the state average at $3.94, while the Little Rock-North Little Rock metro has a $3.83 average.
The national average for a gallon of regular is $4.27, according to AAA.
California, Hawaii, Washington, Nevada and Oregon had the nation's highest gas prices, while North Carolina, Georgia, Texas, Tennessee and Louisiana had the lowest. Arkansas ranked among the 10 least expensive gasoline markets at $3.88 per gallon.
AAA reported that high crude oil prices continue to limit relief at the pump, with oil nearing $100 per barrel amid instability in the Strait of Hormuz. October is on track to become the most expensive October on record for gas prices, following record highs in August and September.
